name: Longer multi-step chain with mixed tool types
user_input: Read data/sample/meeting_notes.md, extract every action item with an owner, write them to notes/action_items.md, and then summarise that list into a single sentence.

expected_plan.notes: A four-step chain where each step depends on the previous. The final summary must be derived from the written file, not from the in-memory extraction, so that the write is genuinely exercised.

ground_truth.note: Six action items in the 'Action items' table of the sample meeting notes. Action item 1 is owned by Priya Raman and action item 6 is also owned by Priya Raman, so owner counts are: Priya Raman 2, Sofia Almeida 1, Kenji Nakamura 1, Grace Oyelaran 1, Tom Whitfield 1.

expected_output_criteria: notes/action_items.md exists and lists every action item with an owner.
The number of action items matches the source document.
The final one-sentence summary is derived from the written file.
Every step's output is verified independently.
failure_conditions: An action item present in the source is missing from the file.
An owner is attributed that does not appear in the source.
The final summary is generated from the pre-write extraction rather than the file.
The chain is executed out of dependency order.

evaluation_criteria.task_completion: Run reaches the success terminal state with the file written and the summary produced.
evaluation_criteria.planning_quality: Plan schema valid; the four steps form a linear dependency chain with no gaps.
evaluation_criteria.tool_selection_accuracy: All four tools are selected; no step is collapsed into another, and no step is skipped.
evaluation_criteria.verification_accuracy: Each of the four steps is verified; verification of the write step compares file content, not the tool's return value.
evaluation_criteria.recovery_effectiveness: Not applicable: no failure is injected in the base run. Recorded as null, not zero.
evaluation_criteria.evidence_accuracy: At least 80% of cited spans from meeting_notes.md support the extracted action items.
evaluation_criteria.execution_time: Wall-clock time from goal intake to terminal state is recorded. No pass/fail threshold applies; execution time is a trade-off metric, reported alongside task completion.

adversarial_notes: Longer chains compound errors: a single mis-extracted item propagates through the write and the summary, and a hybrid system that verifies only the final output can end the run with a confidently wrong summary. A rule-based baseline with a fixed extraction pattern may produce a more accurate list on this specific document than an LLM-based extractor, which is a genuine and reportable finding about the limits of the LLM component. The scenario also tests the max_execution_steps limit, so a hybrid system that over-fragments the plan is penalised.
